files.old: {"16134179":{"kind":"cohort","limitations":["The major limitation is the retrospective design.","Because the study is retrospective and non-randomised, some subgroups contain too few patients for meaningful statistical analysis.","The lack of a uniform imaging protocol for detecting extrahepatic metastatic disease, and variability in how often follow-up imaging was obtained, may have affected both the response and the survival analyses.","The choice between embolisation and chemoembolisation was left to the discretion of the referring physician.","In the islet cell cohort the chemoembolisation group had more resected primary tumours, less extensive liver involvement and more sessions than the embolisation group, so the authors say the apparent chemoembolisation advantage must be viewed with caution.","Direct comparison with the published series they tabulate is described as problematic because of marked heterogeneity in patient groups, treatment protocols and methods of reporting response.","They cannot rule out that patients whose primary tumour had been resected had less local tumour burden, the selection bias others have raised about that comparison.","The conclusions need validation in prospective randomised studies and may change with newer chemotherapeutic agents.","Whether concomitant octreotide with embolisation offers any benefit requires a prospective randomised trial."],"critique":["Progression-free survival is defined in a way that mixes events with censoring: the interval from first embolisation to progression in patients who progressed, or to death or last follow-up in those who did not. Death without documented progression is therefore handled as the end of follow-up rather than as a competing event, and only progression in the liver counts.","Progressive disease is defined against the nadir, as a 25% increase over the measurement at the time of maximal tumour shrinkage, not against baseline. With follow-up imaging at 3 to 4 months then every 4 to 6 months and varying in practice, both response duration and progression-free survival depend on the imaging interval as much as on the disease.","Response was scored by the investigators on non-blinded, non-centrally reviewed CT or MRI using the WHO product of two diameters, in up to five lesions selected by the investigators for their suitability for accurate repeated measurement, in a liver that had just been embolised and was often necrotic.","Not one carcinoid patient achieved a complete response, so the 66.7% response rate consists entirely of partial responses by a bidimensional size criterion, and it is this number the paper uses to prefer bland embolisation.","The survival analysis quietly drops 8 patients lost to follow-up, 4 from each group, while the response rates are reported on the full 69 and 54. The denominators behind the two headline comparisons are therefore different.","The paper's own central finding is internally inconsistent and the inconsistency is not addressed: in carcinoid tumours chemoembolisation halved the response rate (44.4% versus 81.0%, P=0.004) yet made no difference whatever to progression-free or overall survival. If a bidimensional response at this magnitude means anything, the survival curves should separate.","Male sex is presented as the sole independent predictor of survival in carcinoid patients on a relative risk of 2.55 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.99 to 6.58, an interval that includes 1, at P=0.05. The bone-metastasis predictor in islet cell tumours (RR 3.23, 95% CI 1.09-9.53) is barely more robust, and both come from models into which variables were admitted at a univariate threshold of P<0.1 pooled across the two tumour groups.","The recommendation that patients with over 75% liver involvement can still benefit rests on 14 carcinoid patients with a 43% response rate and a 20.1-month median survival, set against a major complication rate of 27.3% versus 12.9% at P=0.11. A non-significant safety comparison in a small subgroup is read as reassurance.","Table 9 pools 13 published series spanning 1983 to 2003 and computes unweighted arithmetic averages of response (32% for chemoembolisation versus 55% for embolisation in carcinoid) across different eras, agents and response criteria. The authors note in the text that such comparison is problematic and then present the averages as corroboration.","The conclusion that concomitant octreotide prolongs progression-free survival comes from an exposure driven entirely by indication: octreotide was given before embolisation to patients with hormonal symptoms, and carcinoid patients were significantly more likely to have received it. The comparison is between patients selected for a syndrome and those without one.","Extrahepatic disease, including the bone metastases that become an independent predictor, was ascertained from whatever bone scans, octreoscans, MRI or CT happened to be available, many performed at outside institutions. A prognostic factor is thus derived from an exposure whose measurement the authors themselves list as a limitation.","Neither grade nor Ki-67 is reported anywhere. 'Carcinoid' pools 43 small-bowel, 9 bronchial and 17 other primaries, and the islet cell group pools 20 functional with 34 non-functional pancreatic tumours, so the two arms of the paper's central comparison are each internally heterogeneous on the axes that now determine treatment.","The indication for treatment was not clear from the record in 9 of 54 islet cell patients, who are nonetheless counted in both the response and survival analyses.","The interventions are not specified at the patient level. Bland embolisation used polyvinyl alcohol particles or gelfoam powder interchangeably, injected to substantial flow slowing judged by the operator, and the chemotherapy regimens used in the chemoembolisation arm are not broken down, so neither arm of the comparison describes a reproducible procedure.","The 8.5% serious-adverse-event rate per session and the single day-3 death are reported for the cohort as a whole, with no breakdown by embolisation versus chemoembolisation, which is precisely the comparison the paper exists to make.","Hormonal response is never measured. Repeat sessions were triggered by 'inadequate hormonal response', an undefined clinical judgement, and no symptom score, chromogranin or 5-HIAA outcome is reported.","No funding statement and no conflict-of-interest declaration appears anywhere in the paper, and a PubMed search found no linked editorial or comment."],"n":"123 patients with histologically confirmed neuroendocrine liver metastases, 69 carcinoid and 54 pancreatic islet cell, treated by hepatic arterial embolisation or chemoembolisation at one tertiary centre between January 1992 and December 2000; 8 patients (4 in each group) were lost to follow-up and dropped from the survival analysis.","bottom_line":"This is the largest single-centre comparison of bland embolisation with chemoembolisation in neuroendocrine liver metastases and the source of the widely quoted claim that adding intra-arterial chemotherapy helps pancreatic but not carcinoid primaries: response 81% versus 44% favouring bland embolisation in carcinoid, and 50% versus 25% favouring chemoembolisation in islet cell tumours. Neither finding is a treatment effect, because the choice between the two was made by the referring physician, and in the islet cell cohort the chemoembolisation group had more resected primaries, less liver disease and more sessions. The response difference in carcinoid produced no difference at all in progression-free or overall survival, which the paper reports without reconciling, and grade, Ki-67 and any symptom measure are absent throughout."},"17629995":{"kind":"case-series","limitations":["The paper carries no limitations section; the concessions below are scattered through the discussion and conclusions.","The authors state it is not possible to make direct comparisons with resection, chemoembolisation and cryoablation series because of the difference in the patients treated.","They concede the cohort is a selected referral population with more aggressive tumour biology, since many had already progressed on octreotide, chemoembolisation, chemotherapy or interferon.","They acknowledge that most liver progression was the development of new lesions or growth of sub-centimetre lesions deliberately left untreated at the index ablation, so the procedure is debulking rather than cure.","They concede that octreotide response is lost early, with over half of patients tolerant within 4 months and most resistant within a year, which is the background against which their symptom-control figures should be read.","They state the male-sex finding is biologically unexplained and can only be analogised to thyroid cancer, and call for further investigation of more aggressive treatment in men."],"critique":["The number of treated metastases is irreconcilable within the paper. The abstract and Table 1 give 384 lesions, the results text says 452, and Table 1's mean of 6 plus or minus 0.5 lesions across 63 patients implies about 378. The per-lesion local recurrence rate of 6.3% depends on which denominator is used.","The entire univariate predictor table is built on 62 patients, not 63, and the sex split changes between tables: Table 1 and the results give 41 men and 22 women, Table 6 gives 41 and 21. Extrahepatic disease is present in 24 patients (38.1%) in the text and Table 3 but in 21 patients in Table 6, and the chromogranin A rows sum to only 41 patients.","The multivariable Cox model carries four covariates on 25 deaths, with candidates admitted on a univariate screen at P<.10, and both significant hazard ratios have confidence intervals that barely clear 1 (1.1 to 9.1 and 1.1 to 10.1). That pattern is what referral timing rather than biology would produce.","This cohort is a subset of the same group's later 89-patient series, and the two papers reach opposite conclusions on the strongest variable: extrahepatic disease has no effect here (P=.85) and is the most significant predictor there (P=.0001, median 26 versus 133 months).","A core-needle biopsy of a representative lesion was taken under ultrasound in every patient to confirm histology, and no grade, Ki-67, mitotic rate or differentiation is reported anywhere. Tissue was in hand and the variable that now governs management of these patients was not measured.","The study is described as a phase II protocol, yet no prespecified primary endpoint, sample size calculation or protocol-defined response criteria appear. The patients excluded are those who were lost or died earliest, which is the group whose disease was progressing fastest.","The median duration of symptom control is calculated on the 33 responders only, dropping the 2 non-responders, and is reported as a median plus or minus a standard error of the mean. Symptom response itself was graded at one week as complete, significant, moderate or minimal by unblinded surgeon assessment, with no definitions and no instrument.","The finding that repeat ablation did not reduce survival is confounded by design. The methods state that patients with numerous, diffuse and rapidly progressing lesions were recommended for alternative therapy, so the worst progressors were channelled out of the repeat-ablation group before the comparison was made.","Table 6's progression stratum compares progression within 6 months against progression after 12 months, omitting entirely the patients who progressed between 6 and 12 months, and concludes that timing of progression does not affect survival.","Survival is reported from three different time zeros (11.0, 5.5 and 3.9 years) against a mean follow-up of only 2.8 plus or minus 0.3 years, so the 5-year rates and the unreached medians for women and for lesions under 3 cm are extrapolations beyond the observed data.","The 48% five-year survival after ablation is set against a cited 61% after resection and discussed as underscoring the place of RFA; the comparison runs the wrong way and the paper does not say so.","The cohort includes 9 medullary thyroid cancers, 4 bronchial carcinoids and 1 undifferentiated neuroendocrine tumour, so almost a quarter of the series lies outside the gastroenteropancreatic population to which the conclusions are applied.","The ablation catheter is a named commercial device (RITA Medical Systems) and two of the cited supporting references are the same authors' own clinical evaluations of that manufacturer's catheter. The paper carries no funding statement and no conflict-of-interest declaration.","A search of PubMed found no linked editorial or comment for this paper, and unlike the authors' 2010 series no podium discussion is printed with it, so no external appraisal is available."],"n":"63 patients with 384 neuroendocrine liver metastases treated in 80 laparoscopic ablation sessions, selected from 524 patients with 1636 primary and secondary liver tumours ablated by one surgeon between January 1996 and October 2005.","bottom_line":"This shows that laparoscopic radiofrequency ablation can be delivered to unresectable, liver-dominant neuroendocrine metastases with 5% morbidity, no deaths, a 1.1-day stay and symptom relief in 94% of symptomatic patients lasting a median of 11 months. It does not show that ablation changes the course of the disease: 80% of imaged patients developed new or progressive liver disease, the survival figures are quoted from three different starting points against a mean follow-up of 2.8 years, and the two independent predictors rest on a four-covariate model with 25 deaths and confidence intervals that barely exclude 1. Tissue was biopsied in every patient and grade was never reported, so the series cannot be read onto the G1/G2 distinctions that now decide who is offered ablation."},"18525307":{"kind":"cohort","limitations":["As a retrospective review from multiple centres the data are incomplete, and the authors state they are continuing the collaboration to capture the proportion of patients symptomatic before and after treatment, the duration of symptomatic and radiographic response, and tumour marker response.","Imaging technique was not standardised and a single response system was not applied; where WHO or RECIST criteria could not be used because the pre- and post-treatment imaging differed, a best estimate of response was given.","The authors name standardising the imaging technique, the response system and the interval between scans in the first 6 months as work still to be done.","No quality-of-life measures were collected; the authors note that EORTC global and liver-specific tools should be included in future analyses of radioembolisation.","Participation was voluntary and, the project being unfunded, the response to join was modest; institutions in Australia and Asia were not approached at all, for want of established relationships.","Specific data could not be found for some patients, so every result is reported as the number with data available over the total possible.","The partition method of activity calculation cannot be applied in neuroendocrine metastases because it requires a single well-defined tumour, so body surface area dosimetry was used throughout."],"critique":["The response percentages are computed over a denominator that includes the treatments that could not be assessed. Only 168 of 185 treatments were assessable, yet partial response is given as 112/185 (60.5%), complete response 5/185, stable disease 42/185 and progression 9/185, so the four categories sum to 90.8% and the 17 unassessable treatments silently dilute every rate.","Response is reported per treatment rather than per patient, so the 22.3% of patients retreated and the centres that deliberately treat one lobe then the other contribute two or three response observations each to a denominator of 185 treatments in 148 people.","The toxicity accounting does not close either. Grade 3 to 4 data were available for 161 of 185 treatments, the rates are nonetheless given over 185, and the statement that no grade 3 to 4 toxicity occurred in 124 of 185 treatments leaves 61 treatments unaccounted for by the handful of listed events.","The median survival of 70 months is reported with 77.7% of patients still alive and a median follow-up of 42 months. The estimate therefore comes from the far tail of a heavily censored curve, and no confidence interval and no numbers at risk are given anywhere.","Survival is timed from the first microsphere treatment in a cohort that, by the stated inclusion criterion, had already completed comprehensive evaluation and treatment of the primary tumour and its metastases. These are survivors of earlier therapy, and prior treatment is nowhere quantified, so the line of therapy this 70-month figure represents is unknown.","The methods define a four-level tumour marker response scale using chromogranin A, serotonin and occasionally 24-hour 5-HIAA, and no marker result appears anywhere in the paper. The stated threshold was 20% and patients were treated with shunt fractions up to 34.1%; how many, and what happened to them, is not reported.","Delivered activity ranged from 38.1% to 147.4% of the body-surface-area prescription, and that percentage was recorded for only 132 of 185 procedures. A delivery of nearly one and a half times the prescribed activity is neither flagged as a deviation nor related to the toxicity data, and the reasons for reduced delivery were not captured.","The safety claim rests on a dosimetry method chosen precisely so that dose need not be measured. Body surface area prescribing is a manufacturer-suggested convention and the paper reports no absorbed dose to tumour or to uninvolved liver, so 'no radiation-induced liver disease' is a statement about clinical observation with no dose denominator behind it.","Radiation-induced liver injury in this disease is a late effect and this cohort is young in follow-up terms, with 78% alive at a median of 42 months. The efficacy figures should not be carried further than that: a 63% objective response is scored per treatment on non-standardised imaging with a best-estimate category where RECIST could not be applied, the percentages are computed over a denominator that includes unassessable treatments, and the 70-month median survival comes from a curve on which 78% of patients were still alive at a median follow-up of 42 months. With no comparator, no quality-of-life data, no tumour-marker results despite a defined scale for them, and no grade or Ki-67, it cannot say what radioembolisation adds or to whom.","funding":"The authors describe the project as unfunded, which is why participation was limited; no funding statement and no conflict-of-interest declaration appears anywhere in the paper."},"19704057":{"kind":"rct","limitations":["Treatment after progression was at the discretion of each centre; most placebo patients went on to a somatostatin analogue and many on the active arm continued it, so long-term observation of patients not receiving octreotide LAR is difficult and no conclusion about overall survival can be drawn from this trial.","The protocol specified that the analysis of time to tumour-related death be based on 121 events; because of the observed effect on tumour growth and a slow recruitment rate the authors stopped further enrolment, without unblinding the nine patients still on treatment.","The number of patients with high hepatic tumour burden was low, and the authors state that the role of hepatic tumour load needs investigating in more depth.","Whether the favourable effect on time to tumour progression translates into prolonged overall survival, an important secondary aim, could not be determined.","Whether patients with a high hepatic tumour burden that developed slowly respond more favourably to biotherapy requires further study.","The result applies to midgut primaries only; the authors call for studies in neuroendocrine tumours of other origins."],"critique":["The effect size comes from an interim analysis at a prespecified local alpha of 0.0122, after which recruitment was stopped because the result was positive. A trial halted early on an efficacy boundary systematically overstates the treatment effect, and PROMID enrolled 85 of a planned 162 patients, so its hazard ratio of 0.32 to 0.34 is the most favourable point in the trial's history rather than its final estimate.","Three different hazard ratios are available for the same comparison (conservative intent-to-treat 0.34, planned intent-to-treat 0.32, per-protocol 0.24), and the subgroup analyses most often quoted in clinical discussion come from the per-protocol set, the most selected of the three.","The subgroup results that drive practice cannot exclude no effect. The hazard ratio of 0.17 at 0 to 10% liver involvement comes from strata of roughly 7 to 14 patients, while the intervals at 10 to 50% (0.10 to 1.67) and above 50% (0.11 to 4.45) include both large benefit and substantial harm, and no interaction test is reported. The claim that octreotide LAR is the treatment of choice in low hepatic load rests on a comparison the trial was never powered to make.","Resection of the primary (HR 0.16 against 0.84 unresected) is similarly exploratory and is confounded with disease extent, since patients whose primary was resectable are not the same patients as those whose was not.","Progression was read by bidimensional WHO criteria, which register a given amount of growth as a larger percentage change than unidimensional RECIST. CLARINET's authors made precisely this point about PROMID, and it is one reason the 6.0-month placebo median here sits so far from CLARINET's 18.0 months.","The primary endpoint is time to tumour progression, not progression-free survival, so deaths without documented progression are censored rather than counted as events. In a disease whose patients die of liver failure, that choice is not neutral.","Nothing in the symptom or quality-of-life data supports the drug. No difference reached significance in the EORTC QLQ-C30 scores, symptomatic response or biochemical response tables, with p values as high as .1106, in a trial that includes functioning tumours and a drug whose original indication is symptom control.","The population is close to the most indolent that exists: 95% had a Ki-67 of 2% or less, 61% had 10% or less liver involvement, 66% had the primary resected, and all were treatment-naive with no curative option. Grade 2 midgut disease and any pancreatic primary are outside the evidence entirely.","With 16 deaths the survival comparison carries no information (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.30 to 2.18), and the placebo median of 73.7 months is longer than the trial could observe, so the figure most often used to characterise untreated midgut NET comes from an immature curve.","The conclusion extends the result to a population the trial never contained: the authors propose octreotide LAR as an attractive option after cytoreductive surgery with few remaining metastases, when PROMID excluded patients with any curative option and performed no liver surgery as part of the study.","Five of the six gallstone events occurred on octreotide and five patients stopped the drug for adverse events against none on placebo, in a population who may subsequently require hepatectomy or hepatic arterial therapy. The safety paragraph records similar serious-adverse-event counts and no treatment-related deaths without drawing that implication.","The trial ran at 18 academic centres in a single country over seven years, averaging under one patient per centre per year, and ended with 9 patients still blinded and on treatment, so the dataset is incomplete by design and cannot be completed.","Novartis, which markets octreotide LAR, funded the trial, supplied the drug and participated in developing the study design, and the disclosure block lists Novartis honoraria for three authors and Novartis research funding for four. Its full text was not obtained, so none of the points above draws on it."],"n":"85 treatment-naive patients with well-differentiated, locally inoperable or metastatic midgut neuroendocrine tumours randomised 1:1 at 18 German academic centres between March 2001 and January 2008, out of 90 enrolled and against a planned sample of 162; reported at the planned interim analysis after 67 progressions and 16 deaths, with 9 patients still on treatment and never unblinded.","bottom_line":"PROMID is the trial that converted somatostatin analogues from symptom control into antitumour therapy, showing a median time to tumour progression of 14.3 against 6.0 months with a hazard ratio of about 0.33 in treatment-naive metastatic midgut NET. The benefit is concentrated where the disease is least threatening, with hazard ratios of 0.17, 0.40 and 0.71 across 0-10%, 10-50% and over 50% hepatic involvement on strata of a dozen patients, so the trial's own data argue that a patient with a heavy liver burden is the one it speaks least to.","funding":"Supported by grants from Novartis, Nuremberg, Germany, which participated in developing the study design and provided the active medication and the funding but, per the paper, took no part in data collection, analysis or interpretation. 64 had a single session, 19 had two, 4 had three and 1 had four.","bottom_line":"This establishes that laparoscopic radiofrequency ablation of neuroendocrine liver metastases is safe and durably palliative in experienced hands, with 5.6% morbidity, a 1.1-day stay, 97% at least partial symptom relief and 92% per-lesion local control in the largest series assembled. It establishes nothing about survival benefit: the 6-year median and 57% five-year figures come from a single arm selected for under 20% liver volume, at most 15 lesions and liver-dominant disease, timed from the ablation rather than from diagnosis, with octreotide, repeat ablation, chemotherapy and embolisation layered on afterwards. Because differentiation and Ki-67 were never examined, the cohort cannot be mapped onto the grade distinctions that now determine which of these patients should be ablated at all."},"21306237":{"kind":"rct","limitations":["The paper has no limitations section; the concessions below are made within the discussion.","The authors acknowledge that early termination of clinical trials may result in overestimation of the true treatment effect and in lower-than-anticipated numbers of enrolled patients.","The trial was terminated early because of the risk of serious adverse events, disease progression and death among patients receiving placebo, that is on the strength of harm in the control arm rather than only on efficacy.","The blinded independent central review that supports the investigator-assessed primary endpoint was retrospective and covered only 49% of patients (84 of 171).","The exploratory subgroup analysis contained small numbers of patients in some subgroups.","Numerical between-group differences in some baseline characteristics were present, which the authors address with post hoc testing rather than adjustment.","Most sunitinib-related adverse events required dose interruption or modification to manage."],"critique":["The headline result did not formally cross the trial's own threshold. The observed test statistic for progression-free survival was z = 3.85 against a prespecified Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming boundary of 3.88, and the trial was stopped anyway. The reported P value of less than 0.001 should be read against that boundary, not against 0.05.","The trial was halted at half its planned size, 171 of 340 patients and 81 of 260 events, so the effect estimate is both the maximum observed and the least precise the protocol contemplated.","Censoring runs in opposite directions in the two arms. Progression-free survival data were censored in 65% of sunitinib patients against 40% on placebo, and 48% of sunitinib patients left the trial because it was terminated against 19% on placebo. Differential censoring of this size is not neutral with respect to the curve that produced the hazard ratio.","The reassurance about baseline imbalance is explicitly unreported. The paper states that univariate and multivariate analysis showed the imbalanced factors had no effect on the progression-free survival benefit, followed by 'data not shown'.","Baseline differences in a randomised trial are handled by adjustment, not by hypothesis testing, and the paper uses post hoc Fisher's exact tests to conclude there were no significant differences in baseline factors. A non-significant p value on a baseline table says nothing about confounding in a 171-patient trial.","The primary endpoint was assessed by unblinded investigators using RECIST, with central review applied retrospectively to half the cohort, in a trial that was unblinded at closure and whose placebo patients were then offered open-label sunitinib.","The survival claim in the final sentence rests on 30 deaths with medians not reached in either arm and 59 of 82 placebo patients crossing over to open-label sunitinib. A hazard ratio of 0.41 (95% CI 0.19-0.89) from that configuration cannot support the stated clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival.","The quality-of-life claim is imported from elsewhere. The discussion cites a recently reported post hoc analysis for a delay in time to deterioration, while this paper's own quality-of-life data show a clinically and statistically significant worsening of diarrhoea by 21.4 points and no difference in global health status.","The observation that other serious adverse events were less common on sunitinib than placebo (26% against 41%) reflects unchecked disease progression in the control arm, and that same observation was part of the justification for stopping the trial. The text gives 4 (13%) in the combination cohort and 16 (18%) in the PRRT-only cohort and cites Table 2, which presents the matched sets of 24, yet 16 of 24 would be 67%; the percentages belong to the full analysis sets and the matched-set figures are never stated.","The ECOG imbalance the authors could not match on is the strongest evidence that the two cohorts were observed differently rather than being clinically different. Performance status was balanced before PRRT and then diverged completely afterwards, with 0% of the combination cohort and 75% of the controls at ECOG 0, which is what prospective trial monitoring against retrospective chart abstraction would produce. The paper acknowledges the possibility and then uses the same observation to argue that its treated cohort was the sicker one.","The argument that the combination cohort had worse prognosis is assembled selectively. More pulmonary metastases are cited as adverse, fewer bone metastases are noted as pointing the other way, extrahepatic disease differed in the full analysis set (83% versus 64%) but was balanced after matching (88% in both), and less liver disease is not mentioned in that passage at all.","Matching discards most of the control pool. Ninety PRRT-only patients were collected and 24 used, with a ten-covariate logistic propensity model fitted across 120 patients to produce those pairs, and no overlap or common-support diagnostics are reported beyond a balance figure.","The combination cohort is defined by having completed and tolerated four full cycles of PRRT and then being fit enough for radioembolisation within 20 weeks. Being alive, non-progressing and well enough for a second procedure is an eligibility requirement in one arm and not the other, however carefully the controls are matched on baseline covariates.","The subgroup numbers do not agree between the results and the discussion. The gastrointestinal and pancreatic subgroups are given as n=10 versus 14 and n=6 versus 7 in the results, and as n=13 versus 15 and n=8 versus 7 in the discussion, for the single finding the paper describes as most interesting.","The benefit is hepatic and the endpoints that matter clinically are unchanged. Median PFS was 30.8 against 30.3 months and median hepatic PFS 33.5 against 30.3 months, with no overall survival difference, so the case for adding SIRT rests entirely on two-year landmark proportions and on a response rate measured in the organ that was irradiated.","Best objective response is the softest available endpoint for this comparison. Radioembolisation produces necrosis and cavitation in treated lesions, and a 71% versus 25% response rate measured by RECIST size change in an irradiated liver cannot be separated from the direct physical effect of the treatment on the target lesions.","No dosimetry of any kind is reported: no absorbed dose to tumour or to normal liver, no dose-volume metrics, in a study of two sequential radiation treatments to the same organ. The authors raise the point themselves as a general deficiency of the field, having run their own study the same way.","The two analyses a clinician would most want, toxicity and hormonal symptom control, were abandoned because the retrospective arm's records would not support them. A combination of two radiation therapies is therefore recommended as safe and feasible on the basis of a comparison in which safety could not be compared.","The funder manufactures the product. The study is funded by Terumo, which makes the holmium-166 microspheres, two co-authors are employed by Medical Affairs Interventional Oncology at Terumo Europe NV and a third is from a commercial biostatistics company, and the conflict-of-interest statement reads that the authors declare no conflicts of interest.","A PubMed search found no linked editorial or comment, so this propensity-matched comparison of a single-arm trial against a historical cohort entered the literature without independent appraisal."],"n":"24 matched pairs: the 30 patients of the prospective single-arm HEPAR PLuS phase 2 trial set against 90 PRRT-only patients collected retrospectively from four European ENETS Centres of Excellence, reduced to 1:1 matching on a ten-covariate propensity score.","bottom_line":"This suggests that adding holmium-166 radioembolisation after four cycles of 177Lu-DOTATATE improves control of liver disease, with two-year hepatic progression-free survival of 82% against 50% and an intrahepatic response rate of 75% against 29% in 24 matched pairs. It does not establish benefit: the primary endpoint is two proportions with overlapping confidence intervals and no statistical test, median PFS and overall survival are unchanged, the combination arm had less liver disease after matching (8% against 20% burden) despite bulky disease being the rationale, and toxicity could not be compared at all. The one arm is a prospective trial cohort that had to survive and tolerate full PRRT to qualify, the other a retrospective chart series, and the study is funded by the microsphere manufacturer with two of its employees as co-authors under a declaration of no conflicts.","funding":"Funded by Terumo, the manufacturer of the holmium-166 microspheres studied. Two co-authors are employed by Medical Affairs Interventional Oncology, Terumo Europe NV, Leuven, and one is from Barton Biostatistics Ltd; the paper nonetheless states that the authors declare no conflicts of interest."}}

  "16134179": {
    "kind": "cohort",
    "limitations": [
      "The major limitation is the retrospective design.",
      "Because the study is retrospective and non-randomised, some subgroups contain too few patients for meaningful statistical analysis.",
      "The lack of a uniform imaging protocol for detecting extrahepatic metastatic disease, and variability in how often follow-up imaging was obtained, may have affected both the response and the survival analyses.",
      "The choice between embolisation and chemoembolisation was left to the discretion of the referring physician.",
      "In the islet cell cohort the chemoembolisation group had more resected primary tumours, less extensive liver involvement and more sessions than the embolisation group, so the authors say the apparent chemoembolisation advantage must be viewed with caution.",
      "Direct comparison with the published series they tabulate is described as problematic because of marked heterogeneity in patient groups, treatment protocols and methods of reporting response.",
      "They cannot rule out that patients whose primary tumour had been resected had less local tumour burden, the selection bias others have raised about that comparison.",
      "The conclusions need validation in prospective randomised studies and may change with newer chemotherapeutic agents.",
      "Whether concomitant octreotide with embolisation offers any benefit requires a prospective randomised trial."
    ],
    "critique": [
      "Progression-free survival is defined in a way that mixes events with censoring: the interval from first embolisation to progression in patients who progressed, or to death or last follow-up in those who did not. Death without documented progression is therefore handled as the end of follow-up rather than as a competing event, and only progression in the liver counts.",
      "Progressive disease is defined against the nadir, as a 25% increase over the measurement at the time of maximal tumour shrinkage, not against baseline. With follow-up imaging at 3 to 4 months then every 4 to 6 months and varying in practice, both response duration and progression-free survival depend on the imaging interval as much as on the disease.",
      "Response was scored by the investigators on non-blinded, non-centrally reviewed CT or MRI using the WHO product of two diameters, in up to five lesions selected by the investigators for their suitability for accurate repeated measurement, in a liver that had just been embolised and was often necrotic.",
      "Not one carcinoid patient achieved a complete response, so the 66.7% response rate consists entirely of partial responses by a bidimensional size criterion, and it is this number the paper uses to prefer bland embolisation.",
      "The survival analysis quietly drops 8 patients lost to follow-up, 4 from each group, while the response rates are reported on the full 69 and 54. The denominators behind the two headline comparisons are therefore different.",
      "The paper's own central finding is internally inconsistent and the inconsistency is not addressed: in carcinoid tumours chemoembolisation halved the response rate (44.4% versus 81.0%, P=0.004) yet made no difference whatever to progression-free or overall survival. If a bidimensional response at this magnitude means anything, the survival curves should separate.",
      "Male sex is presented as the sole independent predictor of survival in carcinoid patients on a relative risk of 2.55 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.99 to 6.58, an interval that includes 1, at P=0.05. The bone-metastasis predictor in islet cell tumours (RR 3.23, 95% CI 1.09-9.53) is barely more robust, and both come from models into which variables were admitted at a univariate threshold of P<0.1 pooled across the two tumour groups.",
      "The recommendation that patients with over 75% liver involvement can still benefit rests on 14 carcinoid patients with a 43% response rate and a 20.1-month median survival, set against a major complication rate of 27.3% versus 12.9% at P=0.11. A non-significant safety comparison in a small subgroup is read as reassurance.",
      "Table 9 pools 13 published series spanning 1983 to 2003 and computes unweighted arithmetic averages of response (32% for chemoembolisation versus 55% for embolisation in carcinoid) across different eras, agents and response criteria. The authors note in the text that such comparison is problematic and then present the averages as corroboration.",
      "The conclusion that concomitant octreotide prolongs progression-free survival comes from an exposure driven entirely by indication: octreotide was given before embolisation to patients with hormonal symptoms, and carcinoid patients were significantly more likely to have received it. The comparison is between patients selected for a syndrome and those without one.",
      "Extrahepatic disease, including the bone metastases that become an independent predictor, was ascertained from whatever bone scans, octreoscans, MRI or CT happened to be available, many performed at outside institutions. A prognostic factor is thus derived from an exposure whose measurement the authors themselves list as a limitation.",
      "Neither grade nor Ki-67 is reported anywhere. 'Carcinoid' pools 43 small-bowel, 9 bronchial and 17 other primaries, and the islet cell group pools 20 functional with 34 non-functional pancreatic tumours, so the two arms of the paper's central comparison are each internally heterogeneous on the axes that now determine treatment.",
      "The indication for treatment was not clear from the record in 9 of 54 islet cell patients, who are nonetheless counted in both the response and survival analyses.",
      "The interventions are not specified at the patient level. Bland embolisation used polyvinyl alcohol particles or gelfoam powder interchangeably, injected to substantial flow slowing judged by the operator, and the chemotherapy regimens used in the chemoembolisation arm are not broken down, so neither arm of the comparison describes a reproducible procedure.",
      "The 8.5% serious-adverse-event rate per session and the single day-3 death are reported for the cohort as a whole, with no breakdown by embolisation versus chemoembolisation, which is precisely the comparison the paper exists to make.",
      "Hormonal response is never measured. Repeat sessions were triggered by 'inadequate hormonal response', an undefined clinical judgement, and no symptom score, chromogranin or 5-HIAA outcome is reported.",
      "No funding statement and no conflict-of-interest declaration appears anywhere in the paper, and a PubMed search found no linked editorial or comment."
    ],
    "n": "123 patients with histologically confirmed neuroendocrine liver metastases, 69 carcinoid and 54 pancreatic islet cell, treated by hepatic arterial embolisation or chemoembolisation at one tertiary centre between January 1992 and December 2000; 8 patients (4 in each group) were lost to follow-up and dropped from the survival analysis.",
    "bottom_line": "This is the largest single-centre comparison of bland embolisation with chemoembolisation in neuroendocrine liver metastases and the source of the widely quoted claim that adding intra-arterial chemotherapy helps pancreatic but not carcinoid primaries: response 81% versus 44% favouring bland embolisation in carcinoid, and 50% versus 25% favouring chemoembolisation in islet cell tumours. Neither finding is a treatment effect, because the choice between the two was made by the referring physician, and in the islet cell cohort the chemoembolisation group had more resected primaries, less liver disease and more sessions. The response difference in carcinoid produced no difference at all in progression-free or overall survival, which the paper reports without reconciling, and grade, Ki-67 and any symptom measure are absent throughout."
  },
  "17629995": {
    "kind": "case-series",
    "limitations": [
      "The paper carries no limitations section; the concessions below are scattered through the discussion and conclusions.",
      "The authors state it is not possible to make direct comparisons with resection, chemoembolisation and cryoablation series because of the difference in the patients treated.",
      "They concede the cohort is a selected referral population with more aggressive tumour biology, since many had already progressed on octreotide, chemoembolisation, chemotherapy or interferon.",
      "They acknowledge that most liver progression was the development of new lesions or growth of sub-centimetre lesions deliberately left untreated at the index ablation, so the procedure is debulking rather than cure.",
      "They concede that octreotide response is lost early, with over half of patients tolerant within 4 months and most resistant within a year, which is the background against which their symptom-control figures should be read.",
      "They state the male-sex finding is biologically unexplained and can only be analogised to thyroid cancer, and call for further investigation of more aggressive treatment in men."
    ],
    "critique": [
      "The number of treated metastases is irreconcilable within the paper. The abstract and Table 1 give 384 lesions, the results text says 452, and Table 1's mean of 6 plus or minus 0.5 lesions across 63 patients implies about 378. The per-lesion local recurrence rate of 6.3% depends on which denominator is used.",
      "The entire univariate predictor table is built on 62 patients, not 63, and the sex split changes between tables: Table 1 and the results give 41 men and 22 women, Table 6 gives 41 and 21. Extrahepatic disease is present in 24 patients (38.1%) in the text and Table 3 but in 21 patients in Table 6, and the chromogranin A rows sum to only 41 patients.",
      "The multivariable Cox model carries four covariates on 25 deaths, with candidates admitted on a univariate screen at P<.10, and both significant hazard ratios have confidence intervals that barely clear 1 (1.1 to 9.1 and 1.1 to 10.1). Table 7's two liver-volume rows carry hazard ratios of 0.9 and 1.8 with identical upper confidence bounds of 2.8, which cannot both be right.",
      "The dominant-tumour-size effect weakens sharply when the survival clock is moved earlier: P=.005 measured from ablation but P=.05 measured from diagnosis of liver metastases. That pattern is what referral timing rather than biology would produce.",
      "This cohort is a subset of the same group's later 89-patient series, and the two papers reach opposite conclusions on the strongest variable: extrahepatic disease has no effect here (P=.85) and is the most significant predictor there (P=.0001, median 26 versus 133 months).",
      "A core-needle biopsy of a representative lesion was taken under ultrasound in every patient to confirm histology, and no grade, Ki-67, mitotic rate or differentiation is reported anywhere. Tissue was in hand and the variable that now governs management of these patients was not measured.",
      "The study is described as a phase II protocol, yet no prespecified primary endpoint, sample size calculation or protocol-defined response criteria appear. The methods promise objective tumour response on serial triphasic CT and no objective response rate is ever reported.",
      "The 80% liver-progression figure is calculated on the 45 patients with at least 3 months of imaging, excluding 18 of 63. The patients excluded are those who were lost or died earliest, which is the group whose disease was progressing fastest.",
      "The median duration of symptom control is calculated on the 33 responders only, dropping the 2 non-responders, and is reported as a median plus or minus a standard error of the mean. Symptom response itself was graded at one week as complete, significant, moderate or minimal by unblinded surgeon assessment, with no definitions and no instrument.",
      "The finding that repeat ablation did not reduce survival is confounded by design. The methods state that patients with numerous, diffuse and rapidly progressing lesions were recommended for alternative therapy, so the worst progressors were channelled out of the repeat-ablation group before the comparison was made.",
      "Table 6's progression stratum compares progression within 6 months against progression after 12 months, omitting entirely the patients who progressed between 6 and 12 months, and concludes that timing of progression does not affect survival.",
      "Survival is reported from three different time zeros (11.0, 5.5 and 3.9 years) against a mean follow-up of only 2.8 plus or minus 0.3 years, so the 5-year rates and the unreached medians for women and for lesions under 3 cm are extrapolations beyond the observed data.",
      "The 48% five-year survival after ablation is set against a cited 61% after resection and discussed as underscoring the place of RFA; the comparison runs the wrong way and the paper does not say so.",
      "The cohort includes 9 medullary thyroid cancers, 4 bronchial carcinoids and 1 undifferentiated neuroendocrine tumour, so almost a quarter of the series lies outside the gastroenteropancreatic population to which the conclusions are applied.",
      "The ablation catheter is a named commercial device (RITA Medical Systems) and two of the cited supporting references are the same authors' own clinical evaluations of that manufacturer's catheter. The paper carries no funding statement and no conflict-of-interest declaration.",
      "A search of PubMed found no linked editorial or comment for this paper, and unlike the authors' 2010 series no podium discussion is printed with it, so no external appraisal is available."
    ],
    "n": "63 patients with 384 neuroendocrine liver metastases treated in 80 laparoscopic ablation sessions, selected from 524 patients with 1636 primary and secondary liver tumours ablated by one surgeon between January 1996 and October 2005.",
    "bottom_line": "This shows that laparoscopic radiofrequency ablation can be delivered to unresectable, liver-dominant neuroendocrine metastases with 5% morbidity, no deaths, a 1.1-day stay and symptom relief in 94% of symptomatic patients lasting a median of 11 months. It does not show that ablation changes the course of the disease: 80% of imaged patients developed new or progressive liver disease, the survival figures are quoted from three different starting points against a mean follow-up of 2.8 years, and the two independent predictors rest on a four-covariate model with 25 deaths and confidence intervals that barely exclude 1. Tissue was biopsied in every patient and grade was never reported, so the series cannot be read onto the G1/G2 distinctions that now decide who is offered ablation."
  },
  "18525307": {
    "kind": "cohort",
    "limitations": [
      "As a retrospective review from multiple centres the data are incomplete, and the authors state they are continuing the collaboration to capture the proportion of patients symptomatic before and after treatment, the duration of symptomatic and radiographic response, and tumour marker response.",
      "Imaging technique was not standardised and a single response system was not applied; where WHO or RECIST criteria could not be used because the pre- and post-treatment imaging differed, a best estimate of response was given.",
      "The authors name standardising the imaging technique, the response system and the interval between scans in the first 6 months as work still to be done.",
      "No quality-of-life measures were collected; the authors note that EORTC global and liver-specific tools should be included in future analyses of radioembolisation.",
      "Participation was voluntary and, the project being unfunded, the response to join was modest; institutions in Australia and Asia were not approached at all, for want of established relationships.",
      "Specific data could not be found for some patients, so every result is reported as the number with data available over the total possible.",
      "The partition method of activity calculation cannot be applied in neuroendocrine metastases because it requires a single well-defined tumour, so body surface area dosimetry was used throughout."
    ],
    "critique": [
      "The response percentages are computed over a denominator that includes the treatments that could not be assessed. Only 168 of 185 treatments were assessable, yet partial response is given as 112/185 (60.5%), complete response 5/185, stable disease 42/185 and progression 9/185, so the four categories sum to 90.8% and the 17 unassessable treatments silently dilute every rate.",
      "Response is reported per treatment rather than per patient, so the 22.3% of patients retreated and the centres that deliberately treat one lobe then the other contribute two or three response observations each to a denominator of 185 treatments in 148 people.",
      "The toxicity accounting does not close either. Grade 3 to 4 data were available for 161 of 185 treatments, the rates are nonetheless given over 185, and the statement that no grade 3 to 4 toxicity occurred in 124 of 185 treatments leaves 61 treatments unaccounted for by the handful of listed events.",
      "The median survival of 70 months is reported with 77.7% of patients still alive and a median follow-up of 42 months. The estimate therefore comes from the far tail of a heavily censored curve, and no confidence interval and no numbers at risk are given anywhere.",
      "Survival is timed from the first microsphere treatment in a cohort that, by the stated inclusion criterion, had already completed comprehensive evaluation and treatment of the primary tumour and its metastases. These are survivors of earlier therapy, and prior treatment is nowhere quantified, so the line of therapy this 70-month figure represents is unknown.",
      "The methods define a four-level tumour marker response scale using chromogranin A, serotonin and occasionally 24-hour 5-HIAA, and no marker result appears anywhere in the paper. The discussion lists marker response among the things the collaboration still intends to collect.",
      "The lung shunt exclusion was breached without separate analysis. The stated threshold was 20% and patients were treated with shunt fractions up to 34.1%; how many, and what happened to them, is not reported.",
      "Delivered activity ranged from 38.1% to 147.4% of the body-surface-area prescription, and that percentage was recorded for only 132 of 185 procedures. A delivery of nearly one and a half times the prescribed activity is neither flagged as a deviation nor related to the toxicity data, and the reasons for reduced delivery were not captured.",
      "The safety claim rests on a dosimetry method chosen precisely so that dose need not be measured. Body surface area prescribing is a manufacturer-suggested convention and the paper reports no absorbed dose to tumour or to uninvolved liver, so 'no radiation-induced liver disease' is a statement about clinical observation with no dose denominator behind it.",
      "Radiation-induced liver injury in this disease is a late effect and this cohort is young in follow-up terms, with 78% alive at a median of 42 months. The same question asked later with longer follow-up found progressive alkaline phosphatase and transaminase elevation and imaging features of portal hypertension after sequential lobar treatment, which this series would not have been positioned to see.",
      "Thirty-three patients had the same liver volume treated two or three times and no cumulative-activity or cumulative-dose analysis is presented, even though repeated irradiation of the same parenchyma is the main theoretical route to late liver injury.",
      "Data were abstracted locally at ten voluntarily participating centres with no central imaging review, no source-data verification and no audit, and every participating team is characterised in the paper as a centre of excellence for radioembolisation. The response and toxicity figures therefore describe best-case expert practice at self-selected sites.",
      "Tables 5 to 8 set the series' own figures beside collected surgical, chemoembolisation, radiopeptide and 131I-MIBG series from the literature without any formal comparison, matching or adjustment, and the discussion draws its favourable reading from those side-by-side tables.",
      "Neither grade nor Ki-67 is reported, 82% of the cohort is recorded only as carcinoid, and the one patient who developed ascites is noted to have had concurrent hepatic progression, so even that single event is attributed away without analysis.",
      "The product studied is a single manufacturer's resin microsphere and the dosimetry follows that manufacturer's recommendation, and the paper carries no funding statement and no conflict-of-interest declaration of any kind; the authors describe the project only as unfunded. A PubMed search found no linked editorial or comment."
    ],
    "n": "148 patients with unresectable neuroendocrine liver metastases treated with resin yttrium-90 microspheres in 185 procedures at 10 North American and European centres, all described as centres of excellence for radioembolisation, with most patients and treatments contributed by half of them; median follow-up 42 months.",
    "bottom_line": "This is the first multicentre series of resin yttrium-90 radioembolisation dedicated to neuroendocrine liver metastases, and what it establishes is tolerability: across 185 procedures in 148 patients, grade 3 to 4 events were uncommon, no radiation-induced liver disease occurred and retreatment of the same volume in 22% caused no liver failure. The efficacy figures should not be carried further than that: a 63% objective response is scored per treatment on non-standardised imaging with a best-estimate category where RECIST could not be applied, the percentages are computed over a denominator that includes unassessable treatments, and the 70-month median survival comes from a curve on which 78% of patients were still alive at a median follow-up of 42 months. With no comparator, no quality-of-life data, no tumour-marker results despite a defined scale for them, and no grade or Ki-67, it cannot say what radioembolisation adds or to whom.",
    "funding": "The authors describe the project as unfunded, which is why participation was limited; no funding statement and no conflict-of-interest declaration appears anywhere in the paper."
  },
  "19704057": {
    "kind": "rct",
    "limitations": [
      "Treatment after progression was at the discretion of each centre; most placebo patients went on to a somatostatin analogue and many on the active arm continued it, so long-term observation of patients not receiving octreotide LAR is difficult and no conclusion about overall survival can be drawn from this trial.",
      "The protocol specified that the analysis of time to tumour-related death be based on 121 events; because of the observed effect on tumour growth and a slow recruitment rate the authors stopped further enrolment, without unblinding the nine patients still on treatment.",
      "The number of patients with high hepatic tumour burden was low, and the authors state that the role of hepatic tumour load needs investigating in more depth.",
      "Whether the favourable effect on time to tumour progression translates into prolonged overall survival, an important secondary aim, could not be determined.",
      "Whether patients with a high hepatic tumour burden that developed slowly respond more favourably to biotherapy requires further study.",
      "The result applies to midgut primaries only; the authors call for studies in neuroendocrine tumours of other origins."
    ],
    "critique": [
      "The effect size comes from an interim analysis at a prespecified local alpha of 0.0122, after which recruitment was stopped because the result was positive. A trial halted early on an efficacy boundary systematically overstates the treatment effect, and PROMID enrolled 85 of a planned 162 patients, so its hazard ratio of 0.32 to 0.34 is the most favourable point in the trial's history rather than its final estimate.",
      "Three different hazard ratios are available for the same comparison (conservative intent-to-treat 0.34, planned intent-to-treat 0.32, per-protocol 0.24), and the subgroup analyses most often quoted in clinical discussion come from the per-protocol set, the most selected of the three.",
      "The subgroup results that drive practice cannot exclude no effect. The hazard ratio of 0.17 at 0 to 10% liver involvement comes from strata of roughly 7 to 14 patients, while the intervals at 10 to 50% (0.10 to 1.67) and above 50% (0.11 to 4.45) include both large benefit and substantial harm, and no interaction test is reported. The claim that octreotide LAR is the treatment of choice in low hepatic load rests on a comparison the trial was never powered to make.",
      "Resection of the primary (HR 0.16 against 0.84 unresected) is similarly exploratory and is confounded with disease extent, since patients whose primary was resectable are not the same patients as those whose was not.",
      "Progression was read by bidimensional WHO criteria, which register a given amount of growth as a larger percentage change than unidimensional RECIST. CLARINET's authors made precisely this point about PROMID, and it is one reason the 6.0-month placebo median here sits so far from CLARINET's 18.0 months.",
      "The primary endpoint is time to tumour progression, not progression-free survival, so deaths without documented progression are censored rather than counted as events. In a disease whose patients die of liver failure, that choice is not neutral.",
      "Nothing in the symptom or quality-of-life data supports the drug. No difference reached significance in the EORTC QLQ-C30 scores, symptomatic response or biochemical response tables, with p values as high as .1106, in a trial that includes functioning tumours and a drug whose original indication is symptom control.",
      "The population is close to the most indolent that exists: 95% had a Ki-67 of 2% or less, 61% had 10% or less liver involvement, 66% had the primary resected, and all were treatment-naive with no curative option. Grade 2 midgut disease and any pancreatic primary are outside the evidence entirely.",
      "With 16 deaths the survival comparison carries no information (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.30 to 2.18), and the placebo median of 73.7 months is longer than the trial could observe, so the figure most often used to characterise untreated midgut NET comes from an immature curve.",
      "The conclusion extends the result to a population the trial never contained: the authors propose octreotide LAR as an attractive option after cytoreductive surgery with few remaining metastases, when PROMID excluded patients with any curative option and performed no liver surgery as part of the study.",
      "Five of the six gallstone events occurred on octreotide and five patients stopped the drug for adverse events against none on placebo, in a population who may subsequently require hepatectomy or hepatic arterial therapy. The safety paragraph records similar serious-adverse-event counts and no treatment-related deaths without drawing that implication.",
      "The trial ran at 18 academic centres in a single country over seven years, averaging under one patient per centre per year, and ended with 9 patients still blinded and on treatment, so the dataset is incomplete by design and cannot be completed.",
      "Novartis, which markets octreotide LAR, funded the trial, supplied the drug and participated in developing the study design, and the disclosure block lists Novartis honoraria for three authors and Novartis research funding for four. The paper states the company took no part in data collection, analysis or interpretation.",
      "A linked editorial accompanies the trial in the same issue (Oberg, 'Is it time to widen the use of somatostatin analogs in neuroendocrine tumors?', J Clin Oncol 2009;27:4635-6, PMID 19704053). Its full text was not obtained, so none of the points above draws on it."
    ],
    "n": "85 treatment-naive patients with well-differentiated, locally inoperable or metastatic midgut neuroendocrine tumours randomised 1:1 at 18 German academic centres between March 2001 and January 2008, out of 90 enrolled and against a planned sample of 162; reported at the planned interim analysis after 67 progressions and 16 deaths, with 9 patients still on treatment and never unblinded.",
    "bottom_line": "PROMID is the trial that converted somatostatin analogues from symptom control into antitumour therapy, showing a median time to tumour progression of 14.3 against 6.0 months with a hazard ratio of about 0.33 in treatment-naive metastatic midgut NET. Its effect is stabilisation, not shrinkage (one partial response in each arm), and it establishes nothing about survival, symptoms or quality of life: only 16 deaths had occurred, the placebo arm went on to somatostatin analogues after progression, and no symptom or quality-of-life comparison reached significance. The benefit is concentrated where the disease is least threatening, with hazard ratios of 0.17, 0.40 and 0.71 across 0-10%, 10-50% and over 50% hepatic involvement on strata of a dozen patients, so the trial's own data argue that a patient with a heavy liver burden is the one it speaks least to.",
    "funding": "Supported by grants from Novartis, Nuremberg, Germany, which participated in developing the study design and provided the active medication and the funding but, per the paper, took no part in data collection, analysis or interpretation. Declared interests: Novartis honoraria to A. Rinke, M. Blaker and R. Arnold; Novartis research funding to A. Rinke, K.-J. Klose, P. Barth and R. Arnold."
  },
  "21134563": {
    "kind": "cohort",
    "limitations": [
      "The paper carries no limitations section; the concessions below are scattered through the introduction, discussion and the printed podium discussion.",
      "Given the complex and select group of patients in this series, the authors state it is not possible to compare RFA directly with other treatment modalities.",
      "Despite 92% local tumour control, new liver and extrahepatic recurrence occurred in about 60% of patients, which the authors read as showing that systemic control of the disease is necessary for overall prognosis.",
      "Liver-directed surgery should be regarded as a debulking operation, as many of these patients have a high rate of recurrence.",
      "The female survival advantage the same group had previously reported held on univariate analysis but disappeared on multivariate analysis.",
      "Asked from the floor whether pathological differentiation, Ki-67 and mitotic rate had been examined, the senior author answered that this analysis was not done.",
      "The authors concede that hepatectomy still has a role in patients with bulky resectable disease too large for ablation."
    ],
    "critique": [
      "The survival analysis loses ten patients without explanation.   "38851203": {

      "The population was not known to be progressing.       "The risk-factor list is assembled from case reports and small series with no multivariable analysis anywhere. Midgut primary, high tumour burden, liver metastases, raised 5-HIAA and chromogranin A, prior carcinoid syndrome, advanced age and concurrent beta-2 agonists are presented side by side as though each had been shown to act independently.",
      "Debulking before PRRT is offered as a recognised preventive measure, which puts a surgeon in the prevention pathway, and no cited series shows that debulking reduces the incidence of crisis. The operative risk of debulking is nowhere weighed against an event rate of 1 to 2%.",
      "The treatment regimen, 500 to 1000 micrograms of intravenous octreotide repeated every 5 minutes until control, carries no dose-finding evidence, no stated ceiling and no defined endpoint of control, for a condition the paper says has no agreed definition.",
      "The two prophylaxis routes recommended are the same manoeuvres the review identifies as capable of blocking tumour uptake, and no threshold of risk is specified at which prophylaxis becomes worth the possible loss of therapeutic efficacy. The reader is told both that prophylaxis is advisable in patients with multiple risk factors and that it may undermine the treatment.",
      "The reassurance that no deaths from this crisis had been reported as of May 2024 is a statement about the published case-report literature in a complication the paper itself describes as under-recognised and undefined.",
      "Guidance elsewhere advises periprocedural intravenous somatostatin analogue for all patients with carcinoid syndrome regardless of long-acting analogue cover, which is more cautious than this review's risk-stratified approach, and the discrepancy is not reconciled.",
      "A PubMed search found no linked editorial or comment, so these recommendations stand unappraised."
    ],
    "n": "No defined review cohort. The institutional component is an audit of 127 177Lu-Dotatate administrations at a single centre between October 2018 and February 2024, in which no carcinoid crisis occurred.",
    "bottom_line": "This is the only dedicated account of carcinoid crisis during 177Lu-Dotatate therapy and it is useful for exactly two things: the risk profile, in which midgut primary and high hepatic tumour burden dominate, and the recognition window, 12 to 48 hours after a dose, usually the first. Everything quantitative in it is weak: the 1 to 2% incidence has no pooled denominator in a condition the authors say has no diagnostic criteria, the paper is narrative despite describing itself as systematic, and the risk factors come from case reports with no multivariable analysis. For a surgeon the load-bearing claim is that pre-treatment debulking is a recognised preventive measure, and no series cited here shows that debulking reduces crisis incidence or that its operative risk is smaller than the event it prevents.",
    "funding": "None declared: the authors state that no funds, grants or other support were received during preparation of the manuscript, and that they have no relevant financial or non-financial interests to disclose."
  },

    "limitations": [
      "The trial was terminated early on the basis of interim analysis results, which the authors acknowledge could lead to overestimation of the treatment effect; they argue the progression-free survival analyses are relatively mature, with 111 of the planned 164 events in the extrapancreatic cohort and progression events in 57 of 95 pancreatic patients.",
      "Placebo rather than an active comparator was used, which the authors justify on the grounds that no therapy has established efficacy after Lu-177 dotatate or targeted agents and that patients could have exhausted all available options before enrolment.",
      "No overall survival difference has been observed, and the authors state the survival data were not mature and may have been affected by crossover and by the high rate of subsequent anticancer therapy.",
      "A majority of patients treated with cabozantinib required dose modification or reduction to manage adverse events.",
      "The authors state that the choice of therapy should be individualised and that future trials on the appropriate sequencing of therapy are needed.",
      "They note that the phase 3 trials supporting everolimus, sunitinib and Lu-177 dotatate largely enrolled patients who had not yet received targeted therapy or radionuclide therapy, so those agents' results do not transfer to this later-line setting."

    "critique": [
      "The trial was stopped on a different endpoint from the one it reports. In May 2023 the data and safety monitoring board recommended that the protocol-specified interim progression-free survival analyses be performed on local assessments because the batched blinded central reads had fallen behind, and the recommendation to terminate followed from those local analyses. The primary endpoint presented is central review.",
      "The alpha spent for efficacy at each interim was 0.001 one-sided, and the published analysis is the post-termination dataset with a data cutoff set to the date of unblinding and crossover. The reported hazard ratios are therefore the effect estimated at the moment the trial was judged positive, with 111 of 164 planned events in the larger cohort.",
      "Follow-up is short relative to what is claimed. Median follow-up was 10.2 months in the extrapancreatic cohort against a cabozantinib median progression-free survival of 8.4 months, and 13.8 months in the pancreatic cohort against a median of 13.8 months. Both primary estimates sit at the edge of the observation window.",
      "The comparator is placebo in a population with a median of two to three prior lines, so the trial establishes activity rather than comparative value. Cabozantinib has never been compared with capecitabine-temozolomide, with another VEGF-receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor, or with PRRT rechallenge, and the paper lists sequencing as an open question while presenting the drug as a new option.",
      "In the extrapancreatic cohort the benefit is almost entirely the absence of progression rather than tumour shrinkage: a 5% confirmed response rate, all partial, against a placebo median progression-free survival of 3.9 months.       "Overall survival shows nothing in either cohort (hazard ratios 0.86 and 0.95), and the explanation offered, crossover in 33% and 41% plus subsequent therapy in 45% to 67%, is itself the reason no survival analysis of this trial will ever be interpretable.",
      "Two thirds of patients could not take the assigned dose. Dose reduction was needed in 66% and 68%, bringing the median average daily dose to about 38 mg against the assigned 60 mg, so the regimen that produced these results is not the regimen that was randomised, and no dose-response or dose-intensity analysis is presented.",
      "Discontinuation for adverse events reached 31% against 15% in the extrapancreatic cohort, and four patients in that arm had a grade 5 event judged at least possibly treatment-related, including two deaths of unspecified cause. For a drug whose benefit is measured in months of radiographic stability, those are the numbers that decide whether it is worth giving.",
      "Quality of life stayed stable and similar between the groups, so a treatment that more than doubles progression-free survival produced no detectable difference in how patients felt, in a trial where two thirds needed dose reduction for toxicity.",
      "Cohort allocation was imperfect in a trial whose two cohorts are analysed independently: 7 pancreatic patients were registered into the extrapancreatic cohort and 3 extrapancreatic patients into the pancreatic cohort, and the extrapancreatic cabozantinib arm had more unknown-primary tumours than placebo.",
      "Grade 3 tumours were eligible and no result is broken down by grade, while poorly differentiated carcinoma was excluded, so the span from grade 1 to well-differentiated grade 3 is treated as one population in cohorts of 95 and 203.",
      "The paper reports no hepatic tumour burden, no site-of-progression data and no liver-specific endpoint, so a trial in a population that is overwhelmingly liver-metastatic gives no information about how cabozantinib sits beside a liver-directed option.",
      "Support came from the National Cancer Institute through Alliance and cooperative group awards and from Exelixis, which manufactures cabozantinib; individual disclosure forms were filed separately rather than printed.",

    "n": "298 patients in two independent cohorts at 62 US sites, enrolled October 2018 to August 2023: 203 with extrapancreatic and 95 with pancreatic well or moderately differentiated neuroendocrine tumours, randomised 2:1 to cabozantinib or placebo within each cohort, all with progression in the previous 12 months after at least one approved line; 59% had already had Lu-177 dotatate.",
    "bottom_line": "CABINET establishes that cabozantinib has real activity after Lu-177 dotatate and targeted therapy, where nothing was previously established, more than doubling progression-free survival in both cohorts (8.4 against 3.9 months extrapancreatic, 13.8 against 4.4 months pancreatic) by blinded central review.
